title: Agentic AI: One Project for Each Phase
design_principles: Build the control loop in raw Python before relying on an orchestration framework.
The model proposes tool calls; trusted application code validates authorization and executes them.
Use one model provider initially and isolate provider-specific calls behind an adapter.
Keep project scope small enough to complete within the assigned week.
Use mock tools for destructive or externally visible actions until approval and security controls are verified.

projects.name: Zero-Framework CLI Coding Assistant
projects.objective: Build a small coding assistant using a standard LLM SDK, Pydantic, Python functions, and a bounded agent loop—without an agent orchestration framework.
projects.problem_statement: Given a task in a sample Python repository, the assistant should inspect allowed files, propose a change, run a fixed test command, observe the result, and stop with a summary.
recommended_stack: One provider SDK: Google GenAI or OpenAI

core_components.name: LLM client adapter
core_components.responsibility: Send messages and tool definitions; normalize provider responses.

core_components.name: Pydantic schemas
core_components.responsibility: Validate tool arguments, agent decisions, and final result structures.

core_components.name: Tool dispatcher
core_components.responsibility: Validate arguments, check permissions, execute tools, and serialize observations.

core_components.name: Agent loop
core_components.responsibility: Repeat model decision, approved tool execution, and observation until final response or budget exhaustion.

core_components.name: CLI
core_components.responsibility: Accept user task and show safe progress and final result.

required_tools.constraints: Resolve paths under a configured workspace root; reject traversal and symlink escapes.
Write only under the workspace; require confirmation for overwriting existing files.
Run a fixed allowlisted test command; do not accept arbitrary shell command strings from the model.

milestones.result: Working LLM adapter and validated Pydantic schemas.
Tool definitions, registry, dispatcher, and structured observations.
Bounded agent loop and workspace-scoped CLI coding assistant.
Integration tests, README, and architecture review.

acceptance_criteria: The model can request a registered tool and receive its result in the next model turn.
Tool arguments are validated before execution.
Unknown tools and invalid arguments are rejected.
File operations cannot escape the workspace.
Only an allowlisted test command can execute.
The loop stops on final response, timeout, or maximum iteration count.
security_and_safety: No unrestricted shell tool.
No production credentials or personal repositories in the workspace.
Do not execute code generated by the model without explicit review.
Keep secrets out of logs.
deliverables: Demo transcript with one success and one failure case

projects.name: Self-Correcting Research and Knowledge Agent
projects.objective: Build a RAG agent that evaluates retrieval quality, performs bounded query reformulation, optionally falls back to external search, cites evidence, and stores selected long-term memories.
projects.problem_statement: Answer questions over a small private document collection while identifying when the collection does not contain sufficient evidence.
recommended_stack: FastAPI optional for a thin API

core_components.name: Document ingestor
core_components.responsibility: Load documents, chunk text, and preserve source metadata.

core_components.name: Embedding adapter
core_components.responsibility: Create consistent embeddings for stored chunks and queries.

core_components.name: Vector retriever
core_components.responsibility: Retrieve relevant chunks with metadata filters.

core_components.name: Relevance grader
core_components.responsibility: Classify retrieved evidence as relevant, partially relevant, or insufficient.

core_components.name: Query rewriter
core_components.responsibility: Reformulate an inadequate query within a fixed retry budget.

core_components.name: External search adapter
core_components.responsibility: Provide an optional fallback behind a provider-neutral interface; use a mock in tests.

core_components.name: Memory store
core_components.responsibility: Persist explicitly selected, user-scoped preferences or facts with inspect/delete support.

required_behaviors: Cite internal document chunks using stable source IDs.
State when the retrieved evidence is insufficient.
Reformulate a query only within a configured maximum retry count.
Use external search only under the defined fallback condition.
Label internal documents and external web sources distinctly.
Separate transient conversation state from long-term memory.

milestones.result: Short-term state model, document chunking, and embeddings.
pgvector storage, retrieval, and cited baseline RAG.
Retrieval evaluation, relevance grading, query rewriting, and optional fallback.
User-scoped long-term memory and integrated agent demo.

acceptance_criteria: A small golden query set maps questions to expected source documents.
Retrieved chunks carry stable source metadata.
The agent abstains or uses the configured fallback when evidence is insufficient.
Retrieval correction has a hard retry limit.
Memory is isolated by user/profile and can be inspected and deleted.
security_and_safety: Treat retrieved documents as untrusted content, not policy instructions.
Do not store sensitive personal data as memory by default.
Enforce user scoping in database queries.
Filter secrets from prompts and logs.

projects.name: LangGraph MCP Multi-Agent Research Workflow
projects.objective: Model a research workflow as a stateful graph and expose selected capabilities through an MCP server.
projects.problem_statement: Given a research question, coordinate research, evidence verification, and report writing; route unsupported claims back for bounded additional research.
recommended_stack: PostgreSQL checkpointer or supported development checkpointer

agent_roles.name: Supervisor
agent_roles.responsibility: Own the workflow state, route work, enforce step limits, and decide when the task is complete.

agent_roles.name: Researcher
agent_roles.responsibility: Gather candidate facts and source references using approved search tools.

agent_roles.name: Fact checker
agent_roles.responsibility: Check whether claims are supported by the supplied source evidence and flag gaps.

agent_roles.name: Writer
agent_roles.responsibility: Produce a concise report that preserves source references and uncertainty.

mcp_capabilities.name: search_sources
mcp_capabilities.description: Search approved sources and return source metadata.

mcp_capabilities.name: fetch_source
mcp_capabilities.description: Fetch an approved source and return relevant content/metadata.

milestones.result: Explicit graph state, nodes, conditional routes, bounded cycles, and error branch.
Checkpoint/resume and approval interrupt prototype.
Supervisor/specialist roles and local MCP server/client.
Integrated end-to-end research report with tests.

acceptance_criteria: The workflow state has an explicit schema.
All graph cycles have bounded exit conditions.
A workflow can resume from a checkpoint using its thread/run identifier.
The MCP client can discover and invoke only intended server tools.
Unsupported claims route back to research no more than the configured number of times.
The final report preserves evidence references and uncertainty.
security_and_safety: Expose read-only MCP tools in this phase.
Use explicit tool allowlists.
Do not treat MCP tool output as trusted policy.
Keep credentials outside graph state and checkpoints.

projects.name: Guarded Research and Publishing Pipeline
projects.objective: Harden the research workflow with server-side authorization, human approval, execution budgets, idempotency, auditability, and adversarial tests.
projects.problem_statement: Prepare a piece of content for publishing, but never perform the publish action unless a valid authorized human approval is recorded for the exact pending payload.
workflow: Publish to a mock target or approved sandbox

controls.requirement: Enforce permissions in tool handlers and backend services, not only in prompts.
Approval is tied to an authenticated approver, approval ID, destination, and exact content/payload hash.
Set maximum graph steps, retries, wall-clock duration, and tool-call limits.
Send only compact, redacted error summaries to the model; keep protected diagnostics in logs.
Treat user content and retrieved sources as untrusted data; enforce tool permissions outside the model.
Use a stable idempotency key and action ledger to avoid duplicate side effects.
Record requester, approver, action, payload reference/hash, timestamp, and outcome.

milestones.result: Permission matrix, approval identity, execution budgets, timeouts, and bounded retries.
Schema validation, safe error recovery, prompt-injection and tool-security tests.
Idempotent mock publisher, audit log, evaluation dataset, and failure simulation.
Integrated guarded workflow and regression report.

acceptance_criteria: The publish handler independently verifies permission and approval.
Approval is invalidated when the pending payload changes.
Rejecting approval never invokes the publisher.
Repeated calls with the same idempotency key do not duplicate the side effect.
Prompt-injection tests cannot expand tool permissions or reveal configured secrets.
Budget exhaustion and tool failures produce explicit terminal or human-escalation states.
security_and_safety: Use a mock publisher by default.
Do not store raw secrets in checkpoints, prompts, or traces.
Require a human to approve public or irreversible actions.
Apply rate limits and destination allowlists before any real integration.

projects.name: Production-Oriented Agentic Research and Publishing API
projects.objective: Package the guarded pipeline as a documented, observable, durable API service with streaming progress and measurable quality.
projects.problem_statement: Provide an API for creating and monitoring agent runs, receiving safe progress events, approving/rejecting pending actions, and retrieving results after restarts.
recommended_stack: One tracing platform: Langfuse or Arize Phoenix

api_surface.purpose: Create an authorized agent run and return a run ID.
Retrieve status and safe progress summary.
Stream user-safe progress events using SSE.
Approve or reject a pending action after server-side authorization.
Retrieve the completed result and source references.

milestones.result: FastAPI run lifecycle and SSE progress events.
Durable PostgreSQL/checkpoint persistence and end-to-end tracing.
Docker image, runtime configuration, health checks, and deployment notes.
Evaluation, latency/cost report, demo, release tag, and documentation.

acceptance_criteria: API requests and responses are validated with explicit schemas.
A run has a stable ID and documented lifecycle states.
Run state and checkpoints can be recovered after service restart.
SSE emits progress/status events but not hidden chain-of-thought, secrets, or raw sensitive tool output.
Approval and authorization from P4 remain enforced through the API.
Traces correlate a run with its model and tool steps while filtering sensitive fields.
An evaluation report includes task success, policy compliance, latency, and cost measurements where available.
A clean checkout can build and run the service by following the README.
security_and_safety: Use runtime secret injection, not Docker build arguments or committed files.
Authenticate users and enforce ownership on all run/approval endpoints.
Apply request limits, provider rate limits, and tool timeouts.
Keep the publisher mocked or sandboxed for the demo unless a real destination is explicitly configured and approved.
Define log/trace redaction and retention.
deliverables: Final demo showing success, rejection, and failure/recovery paths
